agentNote.body:
Ashley — good news on the paperwork, and one thing I still need from you.

Extension of Time Amendment No. 3 is fully signed. You signed it Friday and Christopher Jewett signed it the same day, so our close of escrow is now September 29 and nothing lapsed. The addendum that went with it puts on the record exactly why we are waiting: the home is a manufactured home that was never permanently attached to the land, so it transfers on its own Certificate of Title from the state Department of Housing and Community Development rather than with the deed, and the seller — who bought at a tax sale — has to have that certificate issued in his name first. His application went in July 24 and HCD assigned it for review August 14. They quote eight to ten weeks and they mail the certificate, so I cannot give you a firm day.

The addendum also records something in your favour: that you are ready, willing and able to close, and will close within three business days of that certificate being delivered. So if HCD moves faster than September 29, we close sooner. I want to be straight with you that on HCD's own timeline we may still be filing another extension in late September.

Your money is fine and it is ready — the line of credit against your father's home was drawn August 21 and has been sitting in cash since. There is no lender problem here.

The one thing that still needs doing is the deposit. When you signed Buyer Contingency Removal No. 2 on August 22 you removed every contingency, and neither the extension nor the addendum brings any of that protection back — the addendum only explains the delay. That means your $5,000 is exposed if this never completes. I have an attorney drafting a short, separate addendum that lets you cancel and get the full deposit back if the seller cannot deliver the HCD title. I will send it the moment I have it and I would like it signed before we go much further.

Call me any time.

James Beyersdorf
